task: Edit the wording and control annotations for this fictional macOS application's deletion dialog. Include a title, body, action labels, initial-focus annotation, and keyboard-behavior annotation. Match the explicitly supplied implementation, including no default action; do not infer universal platform behavior. Use clear accessible wording and do not weaken the safeguard against accidental deletion.
input:
Title: Remove saved report?
Body: This will delete the saved report. It can be restored later.
Primary button: Delete
Secondary button: Keep report
Keyboard: Return deletes; Escape closes.

facts.text: The action permanently deletes one saved report from the application.
The application has no undo or restore route for this deletion.
Previously downloaded exports are not affected.
This dialog initially places keyboard focus on its message, not on an action button.
This dialog has no default action button.
Pressing Return at the dialog's initial focus does not activate either action.
Pressing Escape dismisses this dialog without deleting the report.
Deletion requires navigating to and explicitly activating the Delete report button.

forbidden_additions: A default destructive action or deletion triggered by Return at initial focus.
An undo, restore, or export-deletion consequence contrary to the supplied implementation.
A universal claim that Return or Escape behaves this way in every macOS dialog.
Removal of the explicit activation requirement or a claim that the editor tested the interface.
preserve: The safe no-default behavior of this particular implementation.
Permanent deletion distinguished from unaffected downloaded exports.
A clear nondeleting exit and descriptive action labels.
Behavior annotations that can be checked against the supplied facts rather than platform assumptions.
